= {quarkus-cxf-project-name} 3.33.14 LTS release notes

== Important dependency upgrades

* Apache WSS4J 4.0.1 -> 4.0.2 - https://github.com/apache/ws-wss4j/releases/tag/wss4j-4.0.2[release notes], link:https://github.com/apache/ws-wss4j/compare/wss4j-4.0.1+++...+++wss4j-4.0.2[changelog], fixed CVEs (see the https://ws.apache.org/wss4j/security_advisories.html[Apache WSS4J security advisories] for details):
** https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-85532[CVE-2026-85532] Inadequate bounds on derived-key lengths and offsets
** https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-87830[CVE-2026-87830] Streaming policy validation can fail to enforce element signatures and encryption
** https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-88920[CVE-2026-88920] Forged SAML sender-vouches assertions can bypass authentication
** https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-89238[CVE-2026-89238] Incorrect selection of a decrypted header can bypass protection requirements
** https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-92121[CVE-2026-92121] Streaming signature policy checks can be bypassed after processing an STR-Transform reference
** https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-92899[CVE-2026-92899] Alternate nonce encodings can bypass UsernameToken replay detection
** https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-95616[CVE-2026-95616] Malformed X.509 certificate extensions can trigger excessive memory allocation

== Bugfixes

=== https://github.com/quarkiverse/quarkus-cxf/discussions/2320[#2320] `Methods of org.apache.cxf.ws.addressing.ContextUtils not found: $jacocoInit(...)`

Before {quarkus-cxf-project-name} 3.33.14, running `@QuarkusTest` tests with JaCoCo instrumentation could fail during class transformation with the named error.
The transformer expected the synthetic `$jacocoInit(...)` method added to `QuarkusCxfContextUtils` to have a counterpart in CXF's `ContextUtils`.
Since {quarkus-cxf-project-name} 3.33.14, the transformer ignores synthetic methods, allowing these tests to start.

Special thanks to https://github.com/eekhoorn01[@eekhoorn01] for reporting the issue.

== Deprecations

=== WSS4J `BouncyCastleUtils` deprecated

WSS4J 4.0.2 deprecates `org.apache.wss4j.common.crypto.BouncyCastleUtils` for removal.
Use `org.apache.wss4j.common.crypto.X509KeyIdentifierUtil` instead.
The old class delegates to the new one for compatibility.
See the https://ws.apache.org/wss4j/user_guide.html#bouncycastleutils_renamed_to_x509keyidentifierutil[WSS4J migration guide].

== Breaking changes

=== Stricter XPath validation in streaming WS-SecurityPolicy

Before {quarkus-cxf-project-name} 3.33.14, unsupported XPath expressions in streaming WS-SecurityPolicy assertions could silently fail to enforce the intended protection.
Since {quarkus-cxf-project-name} 3.33.14, WSS4J rejects descendant steps (`//`), wildcards, predicates and functions in these expressions.
Use simple element paths, for example `/soap:Envelope/soap:Header/wsse:Security/saml2:Assertion` with the corresponding namespace declarations, instead of `//saml2:Assertion`.
See https://ws.apache.org/wss4j/advisories/CVE-2026-87830.txt[CVE-2026-87830] for background.

=== WSS4J `DOMX509SKI` constructor declares a checked exception

Before {quarkus-cxf-project-name} 3.33.14, `org.apache.wss4j.common.token.DOMX509SKI(Document, X509Certificate)` did not declare a checked exception.
Since {quarkus-cxf-project-name} 3.33.14, this constructor declares `WSSecurityException` for malformed SubjectKeyIdentifier extensions.
Applications calling this constructor directly must catch or declare that exception when recompiling.
See the https://ws.apache.org/wss4j/user_guide.html#domx509ski_signals_a_malformed_subjectkeyidentifier[WSS4J migration guide].
